q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of bolts, nuts and screws per kg?
title: Steel fastener carbon footprint per kg
short: Multiply the wire rod used per kg of fasteners, including scrap, by your steel supplier's factor. Add wire drawing, cold heading, thread rolling and heat treatment energy, then zinc plating or coating. Divide by kilograms dispatched. Steel is usually most of the total; heat treatment is next.
audience: Fastener makers in Ludhiana, Rajkot, Chennai and Pune

ul: Wire rod or bar bought per kg sold, including heading and trimming scrap.
Get a per-tonne figure from the mill; blast furnace, DRI and scrap EAF routes differ widely.
If you export to the EU, fasteners under CN 7318 are CBAM goods, so the importer needs embedded emissions data.
Annealing and hardening furnaces: electricity, PNG or LPG, plus endothermic gas.
Cold heading and thread rolling machines.
Pickling, phosphating and zinc or zinc-flake coating lines.

p: Divide by kilograms of finished product packed and sold, not by raw material bought.

example.title: Worked example: fastener plant per kg (one month)
lines: Hardening furnace PNG: 20,000 SCM x 2.05 = 41,000 kg CO2
Plant total: 147,500 / 300,000 = 0.492 kg CO2 per kg
Add wire rod at your mill's factor for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
